# backupgram

> A Docker image (Bash scripts plus three small Go binaries) that runs automated PostgreSQL backups on a cron
> schedule, with rotating retention, Telegram delivery (Bot API + MTProto),
> optional GPG encryption, webhooks, multi-chat fan-out, auto-discovery of
> databases, an optional HTTP REST control API, Prometheus metrics with a Grafana
> dashboard, off-site copies to S3-compatible storage, and built-in restore tooling.
> Published as `ganiyevuz/backupgram:<pg-version>[-alpine]`.

## Core Files
- [scripts/init.sh]: ENTRYPOINT — validates config, then execs backupgram-api (REST_API_ENABLE=TRUE or METRICS_ENABLE=TRUE; it supervises go-cron) or go-cron directly with SCHEDULE; with BACKUPGRAM_MODE=s3-sync it validates only the S3 settings and execs go-cron with S3_SCHEDULE running scripts/s3-sync.sh (the off-site uploader)
- [scripts/env.sh]: dual-purpose config — sourced for validation/var resolution, executed standalone at startup
- [scripts/backup.sh]: the backup cycle — lock, then per database: dump into a .part file (streamed through GPG when encrypted), verify, rename, link, send to Telegram; then retention, metrics, summary; exits 0 / 1 / 75
- [scripts/lib/]: helpers sourced by backup.sh — layout.sh (folders, links, retention), dump.sh (format detection, streaming dump, verification), discover.sh (database discovery), rls_guard.sh (row-level security checks), metrics.sh (Prometheus output)
- [scripts/restore.sh]: restore tooling — interactive, by file, cross-database, --from-telegram, or --from-s3 (streams from the bucket)
- [scripts/s3-env.sh, scripts/lib/s3.sh, scripts/s3-sync.sh]: off-site copies — s3-env.sh resolves (*_FILE wins) and validates the S3_* settings; lib/s3.sh runs s3-sync and renders the backupgram_offsite_* metrics from its status file; s3-sync.sh is the uploader mode's job (one sync + metrics, exits 1 when the sync failed)
- [tg-upload/]: Go binary (gotd/td) for MTProto upload/download of files up to 2 GB
- [s3-sync/]: Go module (minio-go) — the s3-sync binary: sync (upload what the bucket lacks, then prune by tiers), ls, get, latest; split into a storage interface and pure planning functions
- [rest-api/]: Go module (net/http) for the optional REST control API; layered packages (httpx/config/backups/jobs/handlers/server/supervisor)
- [monitoring/]: Grafana dashboard (grafana/backupgram.json) and Prometheus alert rules (prometheus/backupgram-alerts.yml)
- [tests/]: scenario runner (scenarios.sh), local Docker harness (run-local.sh; includes an S3 test server, RustFS), Pharmakon-shaped PostgreSQL fixture (pharmakon/fixture.sh)
- [hooks/]: run-parts hooks (pre-backup | post-backup | error); 00-webhook implements WEBHOOK_* vars
- [docker/debian.Dockerfile, docker/alpine.Dockerfile]: image definitions; kept in lockstep (identical ENV + symlinks)
- [generate-docker-bake.sh]: source of truth for docker-bake.hcl (generated — do not hand-edit)
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml]: vets/tests all three Go modules, runs scripts against a live postgres:16, then builds/publishes images

## Key Concepts
- Rotation model: each run writes to last/, then hard-links into daily/weekly/monthly/ (same inode, no extra disk); requires a POSIX filesystem with hardlink+symlink support
- Layouts: BACKUP_LAYOUT=period (default: one file per day/week/month) or snapshot (the run's timestamped name in every folder, weekly on Sundays, monthly on the 1st; last/ holds the newest dump of each existing database, and a dropped database's dump and -latest entry leave last/)
- Dump pipeline: each dump goes to last/.<name>.part, is size-checked and fully verified (through the decryption pipe when encrypted), and only then renamed into place; a failure keeps the previous dump. Retention runs once after the loop over every file (one BACKUP_DIR per server/configuration), keeps the copies of databases that failed in the run, and is skipped when no database was backed up
- Encryption: pg_dump is piped into GPG (nothing unencrypted on disk); the key goes through a temp passphrase file, never a command line; directory-format (-Fd) dumps are never encrypted; restore streams the decryption and exits 1 on a wrong key
- Exit codes: backup exits 0 (all databases dumped), 1 (a database failed, the others still ran, or the run aborted), 75 (another run holds ${BACKUP_DIR}/.lock); every file of a run carries the run's start time
- Row-level security guard: BACKUP_RLS_GUARD=TRUE checks each database before its dump (tables the login cannot read in full, or a restrictive policy limiting it) and fails the database, keeping its previous dump
- Metrics: METRICS_TEXTFILE_DIR (node-exporter textfile) and/or METRICS_ENABLE (GET /metrics on REST_API_PORT, unauthenticated; metrics-only mode without REST_API_ENABLE); keep the port internal
- Format branches: gzip SQL (.sql.gz, default), custom (-Fc), tar, directory (-Fd), cluster (pg_dumpall), each optionally GPG-wrapped (.gpg) except directory — kept in sync across backup.sh and restore.sh
- Off-site copies (S3): S3_BUCKET + credentials (S3_*_FILE wins) sync every dump (stamped, encrypted .gpg files in last/ and daily/; no .part, -latest or directory dumps; unencrypted only with S3_ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED=TRUE) to <S3_PREFIX>/<db>/<file> at the end of a backup run, or a separate uploader (BACKUPGRAM_MODE=s3-sync, S3_SCHEDULE, backup folder mounted read-only, no POSTGRES_* and no key; pick one deployment per folder, one S3_PREFIX per server, the same TZ). An upload is verified by size and redone when the size differs; the bucket is pruned by S3_KEEP_DAYS/WEEKS/MONTHS tiers (default BACKUP_KEEP_*), never the newest copy of a database that has a dump in last/; S3_PRUNE=FALSE = upload only. Off-site problems never change a backup run's exit code; the uploader exits 1 after a failed sync. restore --from-s3 <db|key> streams from the bucket; list --s3 [db]; metrics backupgram_offsite_* and alerts BackupgramOffsiteTooOld / BackupgramOffsiteSyncFailed
- Telegram transport: TELEGRAM_UPLOAD_METHOD = smart | botapi | mtproto; 50 MB Bot API limit enforced only against the official api.telegram.org
- Multi-chat fan-out: comma-separated TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID; uploaded once, file_id reused per chat
- Restore by message id: backups embed a 🔖 Restore ID in their caption; restore --from-telegram fetches and restores it
- Secrets precedence: *_FILE (Docker secrets) takes precedence over the plain env var
- Scheduling/health: go-cron (prodrigestivill/go-cron) owns SCHEDULE and serves the healthcheck on HEALTHCHECK_PORT (503 + the last exit status after a failed run; scripts/healthcheck.sh treats exit 75, a locked-out run, as healthy)
- Auto-discover: POSTGRES_DB_AUTODISCOVER backs up every non-template DB (filtered by POSTGRES_DB_INCLUDE globs, minus postgres and POSTGRES_DB_EXCLUDE; databases the login may not CONNECT to are skipped and logged); POSTGRES_DB optional; ignored in cluster mode; an empty discovered set aborts the run
- REST API: optional (REST_API_ENABLE) HTTP control surface behind a bearer token (REST_API_TOKEN); backupgram-api becomes PID 1 and supervises go-cron; long ops run as async jobs (202 + GET /jobs/{id}); listens on REST_API_PORT (8081)
